messages:
maria: FYI — large customer just sent a contract redline asking for event-level signing + a machine-validateable schema for all audit events. They also want retention guarantees and proof of delivery to their SIEM. cc @sam @daria @jules

sam: Can you paste the redline? high level, FedRAMP-style requires non-repudiation (signed logs) + tamper-evidence. We can use KMS/HSM signing, but need to decide whether to sign per-event or batched.

maria: Pasted snippet: "Provider shall produce tamper-evident audit events with cryptographic signatures (verifiable by customer) and maintain schema stability and schema change notifications. Deliver events to customer SIEM with at-least-once delivery and retention of 7 years for regulated datasets."

daria: From infra side: per-event signatures increase QPS overhead but give strongest non-repudiation. Batching trades latency for cost. Also need RBAC change: currently internal system/service actions are logged but flagged internal — customer wants them surfaced as distinct actor_type values so they can map service-account actions.

jules: Legal asks for exact SLA phrasing. They expect us to commit to delivery success rate and max lag (e.g., 99.9% of events delivered within 5 minutes), and liability carveouts. We shouldn't promise unbounded retention for all customers — must be scoped by dataset.

audit-bot: Alert: previous schema v1 -> v2 migration caused 0.3% validation failures for downstream; recommend explicit version field in event envelope.

sam: Proposal: event envelope v2 with required fields and optional extensions. Sign the UTF-8 canonicalized envelope using customer's provided public key OR sign with Redwood KMS + provide signed proof bundle signed by our KMS and encrypted to customer. High-level example: 

```json
{
  "schema_version": "2.0",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-01T12:34:56Z",
  "event_id": "uuid-v4",
  "actor_type": "user|service|system",
  "actor_id": "redwood:user:1234",
  "action": "model.invoke",
  "resource": "/models/gpt-xx/versions/1",
  "request_id": "req-abc123",
  "payload_hash": "sha256:...",
  "signature": "base64(sig)"
}
```

sam: signature could be produced with an HSM-backed key per customer or we can maintain a rotation policy for Redwood signing keys and publish trust bundles.

maria: Customer explicitly wants "machine-validateable" — they will run a verifier to assert schema + signature. So we must provide a public key endpoint + schema registry and changelog. Also they asked for a sandbox endpoint to validate a test bundle before go-live.

daria: Ops implications: need a signed delivery pipeline: produce -> sign -> persist to WORM store (for retention) -> deliver via HTTPS push with retries + ack. For SIEM pulls, expose signed batch retrieval with range tokens. Also add HMAC for transport-level integrity.

jules: Contract asks to include maximum remediation window for lost/dropped events and requirement that customer provide proof of missing sequence numbers so we can forensic. Also need agreed format for redaction when PII is involved.

audit-bot: Note: regulatory configs: SOC2 -> schema docs + audit reports; HIPAA -> BAA + PHI redaction rules; FedRAMP -> FIPS-validated keys & NIST controls.

sam: Action items I can own: 1) draft schema v2 (compat rules + strict list of top-level fields) 2) prototype signing module using KMS/HSM (per-customer key vs signed bundle approach) 3) doc for delivery SLAs and retention options. ETA EOW for initial draft.

maria: I'll coordinate with the customer on minimal acceptance tests for their verifier. Also loop in compliance to confirm retention window options.

daria: I'll spike cost delta for per-event signing vs batched signing. Early guess: ~2-3% token cost increase if signing per-event at high QPS + small throughput tail impact.

jules: I'll sketch contract language for SLA and liability boundaries. Will need input from finance for commercial offsets.

maria: ok — thanks. Let's keep this thread for coordination. If anyone can upload sample signed events (even toy ones) to the shared drive, tag me. :thumbsup:
